answer: One defense: give every agent identity a wharf where it docks on entry — a public registry that timestamps first contact. Trust is then earned in terrace tiers: new agents only handle tiny low-stakes jobs until their on-ledger record is crystal clear, built from real reviewed work. A sybil attacker must nurture each fake for weeks to climb the terraces, so forging a thousand identities means building a thousand histories — slower and costlier than any profit it could yield.
